articleTitle: WAMPAC: The Dream of Perfect System Operation [In My View]
abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) satellite-supported time-synchronized measurements of current and voltage phasors by phasor measurement units (PMUs) were first invented in 1988 by Arun G. Phadke and James S. Thorp at Virginia Tech and made commercially available in the 1990s by Macrodyne. The first wide-area measurement system (WAMS) was put into operation by the Bonneville Power Administration around the year 2000 purely for monitoring purposes. Based on the first PMU, the broader question was how to design PMU-based wide-area monitoring, protection, and control (WAMPAC) systems with beneficial applications for the monitoring, protection, and control of electrical power grids and the aim of increasing grid utilization and stable grid operation. In brief, it was the dream of perfect system supervision and operation far beyond the state of the art of well-established supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems.

articleTitle: Current Status of HVdc Technology [In My View]
abstract: The adoption of high-voltage direct current (HVdc) transmission is rapidly increasing worldwide, with evolving concepts and configurations. Presently, over 250 HVdc systems are operational globally, and numerous new HVdc projects, including both overhead lines and cable systems, are in the planning stages. HVdc technology has been in use for over half a century, initially relying on line-commutated converters (LCCs), also known as current source converters. In the past two decades, voltage source converter (VSC)-based HVdc systems have gained prominence in the power industry, with power ratings now reaching up to 2,000 to 3,000 MW.

articleTitle: Kriegstetten–Solothurn: First Swiss Commercial High-Voltage System [History]
abstract: Switzerland’s first commercially used high-voltage power system with transmission from Kriegstetten to Solothurn was commissioned in 1886. The 2-kV dc system was a pioneering achievement from a technical and historical perspective. The skill and foresight of the pioneers Charles E. Brown and Walter Boveri, who later founded the Brown Boveri company (today ABB), must be recognized. As employees of Maschinenfabrik Oerlikon in Zürich, Switzerland at the time, they succeeded in designing and building an exceptionally well-functioning and efficient power system.

articleTitle: Synchro-Waveforms in Wide-Area Monitoring, Control, and Protection: Real-World Examples and Future Opportunities
abstract: The concept of synchro-waveforms has received increasing attention in recent years in the field of power system monitoring, keeping pace with the changes and the challenges in the power systems and smart grids landscape. The sensor device to record synchro-waveforms may be referred to as a waveform measurement unit (WMU). WMUs record time-synchronized waveform measurements of voltage and current at different locations on a power network.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Operation of the Hellenic Transmission System Through Wide-Area Monitoring and Control: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation of a Phasor Measurement Unit-Based System With Advanced Algorithms
abstract: The escalating occurrences of transmission congestions, overvoltages, undervoltages, power oscillations, and frequency abnormalities in transmission systems underline the need for a comprehensive review and enhancement of traditional management and operation tools and for the creation of new ones able to obtain real-time data from the field for analysis and operation. Jointly with an improvement of the dynamic models of the power grid, this will result in a better understanding of the system behavior especially in critical situations.

articleTitle: A Flexible Low-Frequency AC Transmission System: Principles and Applications
abstract: According to the development and planning of global offshore wind power in recent years, the future developing trend has shown the probability of a system that is a large-scale, clustered, and in a deep open sea area. At present, the wind power resource in coastal areas has been widely exploited, while the offshore wind power resource in the open sea area is relatively abundant, with wider distribution ranges, richer energy resources, and more stable wind power. Since the cost of development is gradually decreased, offshore wind power will inevitably develop in deep open sea areas with higher power rating offshore turbines in the future.

articleTitle: Wide-Area Monitoring Protection and Control Supported Operation and Planning in the Ecuadorian Power System: Improving Security and Reliability
abstract: The continuous operation and planning of electric power systems undergoes several technical and economic changes associated with environmental and societal goals toward clean, affordable, and resilient sustainable energy supply and deployment. This entails diverse upgrades, which include, for instance, integration with other energy sectors and massive addition of renewable power generation, responsive demand, and different types of storage. The dynamic properties and strength of power systems are evolving toward unprecedented levels with lowered sources for the effective management of active and reactive power balancing in different time scales. Thus, the overall security and reliability performance can be seriously compromised as unexpected disturbances may eventually cause violations to the security limits that are established for the electric power system; this may lead to the outage of important system elements and even partial or total blackouts.

articleTitle: World’s First UHV Hybrid LCC–VSC MTDC Project: Experimental Tests and Onsite Commissioning
abstract: The WDD project is the world’s first multi-terminal UHVDC project that combines LCC-HVDC and VSC-HVDC. Such station-to-station hybrid UHVDC systems can make full use of the technical advantages of VSC to ride through the faults of AC system and improve the voltage support capability of power grids at the receiving end. One of the key challenges for the success of this project is to ensure that both the designs of the main equipment and the control functions meet the expected performance indices and technical specifications. For this, before being taken into operation, experimental tests based on a physical prototype followed by onsite commissioning are essential to verify the safety and reliability of equipment and system in various operating conditions. This article aims to introduce the experimental platform, key physical prototype tests based on the platform, and the key tests undertaken during system onsite commissioning.

articleTitle: Best Practice: Grid-Forming Converter Technological Development in Great Britain
abstract: In this article, National ENERGY System Operator (NESO), the Great Britain (GB) energy system operator, aims to share its best practice for the introduction and development of emerging grid-forming (GF) capability for voltage-sourced-converter-based technological applications, including but not limited to high-voltage direct current (HVdc), the flexible ac transmission system, and other converter-based applications within GB energy markets, through its strategic development. In doing so, it will potentially help relevant value chain players explore and evolve regional and even global energy markets for emerging GF converter (GFC)-based technologies.

articleTitle: Applications of Synchronized Measurement Technologies in Power Distribution Systems: Helping to Speed Up Technology Deployment
abstract: Over the last decade there has been increased interest in using synchronized measurement technologies (SMTs) to address distribution system needs. Modern distribution systems include growing penetration levels of distributed energy resources (DERs); photovoltaic (PV) and wind distributed generation (DG), and battery energy storage systems; electric vehicles (EVs); data centers; and more active consumer participation through, for instance, time-of-use rates and demand response. Furthermore, the need for higher reliability, power quality, resilience, and greater situational awareness of the distribution system is driving the increasing utilization of georeferenced and time-synchronized data with high spatial granularity and temporal resolution. This type of data can be used for multiple applications to enhance distribution monitoring, control, and protection capabilities. These benefits have prompted growing interest in the broad-scale deployment of SMTs on the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Enhancing Synchrophasor Reliability Through Network-Based Time Synchronization: KEPCO’s Practical Approach
abstract: Accurate timing services are important for effectively operating power grids. Traditionally, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems make use of time stamps to quickly identify and respond to faults in the event of incidents. However, with the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind, the grid has become more susceptible to even minor disturbances. In response, utilities have begun deploying wide-area monitoring systems (WAMS) to monitor real-time voltage and frequency oscillations, which mainly consist of phasor measurement units (PMUs). These systems require a time stamp at every measurement, with a high level of accuracy, which means that the timing services must guarantee 24/7 availability.

articleTitle: Macrogrids and Supergrids: Wide Area Transmission to Improve Electrification and Variable Renewable Energy Use
abstract: Studies have shown that wide area high-voltage dc (HVdc) electric power grids will be needed for the future. In North America, these are known as “macrogrids” and in Europe, “supergrids,” which are sometimes referred to as “hypergrids.” There are obstacles in the way to achieving these wide area grids, however. What are these obstacles, and how can they be overcome? Such obstacles include passing through multiple jurisdictions and obtaining permitting. The NIMBY challenge is one such issue. Of course, a wide area transmission grid will pass through different countries and states, adding to the permitting challenge. The processes that are being applied include the use of rights-of-way of existing railroads or highways. Underwater locations may include those beneath lakes and rivers as well as those undersea. In the United States, the right-of-way of a rail line is being used to traverse several states for 2,100-MW, ±525-kV HVdc cables. Roadside rights-of-way are also under active consideration for HVdc cables for the macrogrid.

articleTitle: Wide-Area-Measurement-System-Based Event Analytics in the Power System: A Data-Driven Framework for Disturbance Characterization and Source Localization in the Indian Grid
abstract: Dynamic monitoring of power systems is crucial for improved situational awareness and decision-making. This article examines the experience of the Indian grid, using a wide-area monitoring system and advanced analytics, on event detection, classification, and localization. It highlights the need for integrated, multi-module solutions with advanced signal processing and analytical methods for effective monitoring in the changing grid scenario with large-scale inverter-based renewable resources.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing the Grid of the Future With a Wide-Area Monitoring and Control System: Phasor Measurement Unit Applications in Grid Control, Protection, and Event Analysis at Tenaga Nasional Berhad
abstract: This article presents an in-depth exploration of the advancement of the phase measurement units (PMUs) in the wide-area intelligent system (WAIS) program at Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), Malaysia. TNB, Malaysia’s largest electricity utility, is at the forefront of the energy transition, making significant contributions to generation, transmission, and distribution. TNB’s commitment to reliability is demonstrated by its adoption of PMUs to ensure efficient and robust grid operations. The PMU-based energy management system (EMS) at TNB is an integrated system designed to enhance the grid’s monitoring, protection, and control capabilities. It is based on the linear state estimation (LSE) platform and can utilize both streaming and historical PMU data to perform critical tasks, such as bad data detection; event detection; state estimation; and, most importantly, the creation of the PMU-based state estimator cases.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling of High-Power Converters: An Approach for Stability Analysis of HVdc, FACTS, and Wind Power Delivery Systems
abstract: Analytical modeling of converters for FACTS, HVdc, and wind generators in power transmission systems complements detailed EMT simulation and expedites system dynamic studies. It also facilitates parametric studies, and a good example of model use is eigenvalue analysis, which provides fast and comprehensive stability examination and controller design. Another example of model use is the frequency-domain analysis and wider analysis using open-loop block diagrams. This application can lead to more granular examination of control interactions. On the other hand, analytical model building requires key steps and technologies, such as setting up subsystem dynamic equations, carrying out coordinate frame transformation, making an overall interconnected system, and validation. This paper offers a critical review on those technologies and presents several examples (MMC-HVDC, SVC, and wind generators) to demonstrate the key methods as well as the outcomes that help dynamic and stability analysis.

articleTitle: Essential System Services Provided by HVdc Systems: Current Status and Future Opportunities in South Korea
abstract: Achieving zero carbon emissions by 2050 in South Korea necessitates significant restrictions on coal and natural gas power plants, along with increased reliance on renewable energy sources (RES). This transition drives the development of high voltage dc (HVdc) systems to efficiently transmit renewable energy. The intermittent nature of RES leads to real-time power imbalances, prompting research into HVdc systems for essential system services such as frequency control and power balancing. As RES expands, a multi-terminal dc network will be needed to enhance inter-grid power sharing, with centralized and decentralized control strategies managing power flow and grid stability.

articleTitle: Integration of Renewable Energy With Embedded High-Voltage dc Links in Brazil: A Time-Synchronized Angle Difference Controller
abstract: The continental-size Brazilian interconnected power system is divided into four geo-electric regions with different seasonal wet and dry conditions, all synchronously connected by extra high voltage ac lines. This natural characteristic emphasizes the importance of the transmission system among the regions. Bottlenecks in those connections may reflect in local energy shortage in one region and water spillage in another region, since Brazil is still a hydroelectricity powerhouse. Recently, the high share of hydro generation is being reduced, as wind and solar generation have significantly increased. Due to the fast-paced growth of wind and solar generation, Brazil has decided to increase the participation of HVdc transmission between the geo-electric regions, to transfer the surplus of wind and solar generation from one region to another. The growth of renewable energy with its intermittent characteristics, paired with market-based generation dispatch, has put new demands on the control systems of embedded HVdc links. Those uncertainties demand an adaptable HVdc power flow control to avoid adverse effects such as loop power flows and increased transmission losses. Through computer simulation the paper presents a time-synchronized controller that modulates the HVdc power flow setpoints according to the difference of the rectifier and inverter voltage phasor angles. The ongoing installation of phasor measurement units at the HVdc converter stations sets the ground for the planning of a wide-area monitoring, protection and control system able to coordinate the present and future embedded HVdc links.

articleTitle: HVdc and FACTS: Revolutionizing Low-Carbon Electricity Grids [Guest Editorial]
abstract: As the backbone of energy delivery and distribution, electricity grids become increasingly important when we are working toward clean energy transitions. In fact, electricity grids have been in operation for more than 100 years, delivering power to households, businesses, and industry in the most efficient manner. For the implementation of the net-zero target and energy transition, we will need to develop bigger, stronger, and smarter grids.
